(basketball)|Fenerbahçe]] of the Turkish [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL) and the [[EuroLeague]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama Crimson Tide]] and the [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia Cavaliers]]. ==Early life== Key is the nephew of NBA player [[Ralph Sampson]], who starred at the University of Virginia.{{cite web|url=https://www.dailypress.com/sports/dp-spt-uva-hokies-mens-basketball-braxton-key-acc-010919-story.html|title= Virginia's Braxton Key shares special moment with cousin Ralph Sampson after winning national title|first=Josh|last= Needelman|date=April 9, 2019|accessdate=April 9, 2019|work=The Daily Progress}}{{cite web|url=https://www.dailypress.com/sports/dp-spt-uva-hokies-mens-basketball-braxton-key-acc-010919-story.html|title= Key finding his niche for U.Va., which plays Wednesday night at Boston College|first=Norm|last= Wood|date=January 8, 2019|accessdate=April 9, 2019|work=Daily Press}} Key's father Eric Key played at [[Radford Highlanders men's basketball|Radford University]]. Under his childhood surname of Blackwell,{{cite web|url=https://www.tennessean.com/story/sports/2015/10/21/braxton-blackwell-commits/74303064/|title = Braxton (Blackwell) Key commits to Alabama|first=Michael|last=Murphy|date=October 21, 2015|work = The Tennessean|accessdate = February 6, 2024}} Key played three seasons with [[Christ Presbyterian Academy]], leading the team to a state title in 2013 and winning [[TSSAA]]'s Mr. Basketball award in 2014 and 2015.{{cite web|url=https://tssaasports.com/school/?id=594&sportid=2|title = Christ Presbyterian Lions Championship History|accessdate = February 6, 2024| work=TSSAAsports.com}} He then transferred to [[Oak Hill Academy (Mouth of Wilson, Virginia)|Oak Hill Academy]] for his senior year, where he played under his father's surname for the first time and led the team to a 45–1 record and national championship.{{cite news |last1=Doughty |first1=Doug |title=Plenty of Virginia ties drew men's basketball transfer Braxton Key to the Cavaliers |url=https://www.roanoke.com/sports/uva/plenty-of-virginia-ties-drew-men-s-basketball-transfer-braxton/article_245ff40c-bd82-587d-a127-0e1f9579bc00.html |accessdate=April 9, 2019 |work=[[Roanoke Times]] |date=June 29, 2018}}{{cite news |title=Virginia guard Braxton Key granted NCAA waiver, is eligible to play immediately |url=https://www.dailyprogress.com/cavalierinsider/virginia-guard-braxton-key-granted-ncaa-waiver-is-eligible-to/article_50110f9c-d614-11e8-9c65-f7785ab37536.html |accessdate=April 9, 2019 |work=[[The Daily Progress]] |date=October 22, 2018}} ==College career== [[File:Braxton Key (cropped).jpg|thumb|left|upright|Diakite at [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]].]] Key averaged a team-high 12 points and 5.7 rebounds per game as a freshman at [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]]. He scored a season-high 26 points against [[Georgia Bulldogs men's basketball|Georgia]] and was named to the All-SEC Freshman team. As a sophomore, Key averaged 7.0 points, 5.3 rebounds, 1.8 assists and 0.4 blocks per game. He was hobbled by a knee injury that forced him to miss some playing time. After the season, Key transferred to Virginia and was granted an immediate eligibility waiver by the NCAA.{{cite news |last1=Boone |first1=Kyle |title=Why No. 5 Virginia got immediate eligibility for Alabama transfer Braxton Key |url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/why-no-5-virginia-got-immediate-eligibility-for-alabama-transfer-braxton-key/ |accessdate=April 9, 2019 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=October 22, 2018}} In the [[2018–19 Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball team|2018–19 season]], Key won a national championship at Virginia, scoring six points, pulling down 10 rebounds and blocking one shot in the title game against [[2018–19 Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball team|Texas Tech]].{{cite news |last1=Needelman |first1=Josh |title=Virginia's Braxton Key shares special moment with cousin Ralph Sampson after winning national title |url=https://www.dailyprogress.com/cavalierinsider/virginia-s-braxton-key-shares-special-moment-with-cousin-ralph/article_aec68d12-5a9b-11e9-9d39-1fbe512b330c.html |accessdate=April 9, 2019 |work=[[The Daily Progress]] |date=April 9, 2019}} Key averaged 5.7 points and 5.3 rebounds as a junior, starting six games.{{cite news |last1=Flaherty |first1=Kevin |title=Virginia's Braxton Key tapped as potential breakout player |url=https://247sports.com/college/virginia/Article/Virginia-Cavaliers-Basketball-UVA-Braxton-Key-tapped-as-potential-breakout-player-137662665/ |accessdate=November 27, 2019 |work=247 Sports |date=October 29, 2019}} Key had surgery for a wrist injury in November 2019 and missed several games.{{cite news |title=Virginia's Braxton Key out of lineup following wrist surgery |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/28178105/virginia-braxton-key-lineup-following-wrist-surgery |accessdate=November 27, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=November 27, 2019}} He returned to action on December 18 against [[Stony Brook Seawolves men's basketball|Stony Brook]].{{cite news |last1=Conlin |first1=Bennett |title=Braxton Key returns as No. 9 Virginia turns away upset-minded Stony Brook |url=https://www.dailyprogress.com/cavalierinsider/braxton-key-returns-as-no-virginia-turns-away-upset-minded/article_f684a529-8d6f-5963-ba24-9cb3c765d528.html |accessdate=December 31, 2019 |work=[[The Daily Progress]] |date=December 18, 2019}} At the conclusion of the regular season, Key was named All-ACC Honorable Mention.{{cite web|url=https://theacc.com/news/2020/3/8/athlete-awards-2020-acc-mens-basketball-award-winners-announced.aspx|title=2020 ACC Men's Basketball Award Winners Announced|website=theacc.com|publisher=Atlantic Coast Conference|date=March 9, 2020|accessdate=March 9, 2020}} As a senior, Key averaged 9.9 points, 7.4 rebounds, and 1.8 assists per game.{{cite web |last1=Darney |first1=Caroline Darney |title=Diakite, Clark, and Key represent Virginia on All-ACC teams |url=https://www.streakingthelawn.com/2020/3/9/21171506/ncaa-basketball-acc-conference-awards-tre-jones-duke-florida-state-leonard-hamilton |website=Streaking the Lawn |publisher=[[SB Nation]] |accessdate=March 23, 2020 |date=March 9, 2020}} ==Professional career== ===Delaware Blue Coats (2021–2022)=== After going undrafted in the [[2020 NBA draft]], Key joined the [[Delaware Blue Coats]] of the [[NBA G League]] in January 2021, after being selected in the G League draft.{{cite web|title=Blue Coats Announce 2021 Roster|url=https://bluecoats.gleague.nba.com/news/blue-coats-announce-2021-roster/|website=NBA.com|date=January 14, 2021|access-date=October 28, 2021}} On March 2, he posted a season-high 19 points to go with five rebounds, two assists, two steals two blocks in a 120–92 win over the [[NBA G League Ignite]].{{cite news|title=BLUE COATS BEAT NBA G LEAGUE IGNITE FOR EIGHTH WIN|url=https://www.witn22.org/2021/03/02/blue-coats-beat-nba-g-league-ignite-for-eighth-win/|website=WITN22.org|date=March 2, 2021|access-date=October 28, 2021}} On October 13, 2021, Key signed with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]], but was waived the same day.{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Sixers Sign, Waive Jared Brownridge, Braxton Key|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2021/10/sixers-sign-waive-jared-brownridge-braxton-key.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=October 13, 2021|access-date=December 19, 2021}} On October 25, he re-signed with Delaware.{{cite tweet|author=Delaware Blue Coats|number=1452778827533492232|title=Let's go Camping. #TrainingCamp | #GetYourCoatsOn|user=blue_coats|date=October 25, 2021|access-date=December 19, 2021}} In 43 career NBA G League games, he averaged 14.8 points, 6.1 rebounds, 2.9 assists, 1.8 steals and 1.3 blocks in 23.7 minutes.{{cite web|title=DETROIT PISTONS SIGN BRAXTON KEY TO A TWO-WAY CONTRACT|url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-sign-braxton-key-to-a-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=April 3, 2022|access-date=April 3, 2022}} ===Philadelphia 76ers (2022)=== On January 5, 2022, Key signed a 10-day contract with the Philadelphia 76ers.{{cite news|first=Noah|last=Levick|title=Sixers signing versatile Braxton Key to 10-day deal as Reed enters protocols|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/philadelphia/sixers/braxton-key-contract-sixers-blue-coats-nba-paul-reed-nba-covid-19-protocols|work=[[NBC Sports]]|date=January 5, 2022|access-date=January 5, 2022}} Key appeared in two games for the 76ers, scoring two points in six total minutes. After his 10-day contract expired, Key was reacquired by the Delaware Blue Coats.{{cite web|title=2021–22 NBA G League transactions|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=NBA.com|access-date=January 11, 2022}} ===Detroit Pistons / Motor City Cruise (2022)=== On March 24, 2022, Key signed a 10-day contract with the [[Detroit Pistons]].{{cite web|title=DETROIT PISTONS SIGN BRAXTON KEY TO A 10-DAY CONTRACT|url=https://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-sign-braxton-key-to-a-10-day-contract|website=NBA.com|date=March 24, 2022|access-date=March 24, 2022}} On April 3, he signed a two-way contract. On December 26, 2022, Key was waived.{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/pistons-jared-rhoden-signed-by-detroit/|title=Pistons' Jared Rhoden: Signed by Detroit|website=cbssports.com|date=December 26, 2022|access-date=December 26, 2022}} ===Second stint with Delaware (2023)=== On January 1, 2023, Key was re-acquired by the [[Delaware Blue Coats]],{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=gleague.nba.com|title=2022–23 NBA G League Transactions|date=December 31, 2022|access-date=December 31, 2022}} and eventually helped the team win the [[NBA G League]] title.{{cite web|first=Noah|last=Levick|title=Delaware Blue Coats win G League championship; Jaden Springer named Finals MVP|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/philadelphia/sixers/delaware-blue-coats-nba-g-league-championship-2023-jaden-springer-mac-mcclung|website=NBCSports.com|date=April 7, 2023|access-date=April 7, 2023}} ===Vaqueros de Bayamón (2023)=== On April 14, 2023, Key signed with [[Vaqueros de Bayamón]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional|Puerto Rican league]].{{cite tweet|number=1646948574721089546|title=#BSNPR OFICIAL: El delantero Braxton Key es el nuevo refuerzo de los Vaqueros de Bayamón en sustitución del lesionado Jamil Wilson.|user=LaGuerraBSN|author=La Guerra del BSN|date=April 14, 2023|access-date=April 19, 2023}} He was released on May 31.{{Cite web |date=2023-05-05 |title=International and G League transactions log 2023–24: Where are former NBA players going? |url=https://hoopshype.com/lists/international-and-g-league-transactions-log-2023-24-where-are-former-nba-players-going/ |access-date=2023-06-30 |website=HoopsHype |language=en-US}} ===Denver Nuggets / Grand Rapids Gold (2023–2024)=== Braxton Key signed with the [[Dallas Mavericks]] for the [[2023 NBA Summer League|NBA 2K24 Summer League]]. On July 18, 2023, Key signed a two-way contract with the [[Denver Nuggets]].{{cite web|title=NUGGETS SIGN GILLESPIE, HUFF AND KEY TO TWO-WAY CONTRACTS|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-sign-gillespie-huff-and-key-to-two-way-contracts|website=NBA.com|date=July 18, 2023|access-date=July 18, 2023}} ===San Diego Clippers (2024–2025)=== On October 12, 2024, Key signed with the [[Los Angeles Clippers]],{{cite web|first=Arthur|last=Hill|title=Braxton Key Signs With Clippers|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/10/braxton-key-to-sign-with-clippers.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=October 13, 2024|access-date=October 14, 2024}} but was waived a week later.{{cite web|first=Arthur|last=Hill|title=Clippers Waive Elijah Harkless, Alondes Williams, Braxton Key|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2024/10/clippers-waive-elijah-harkless-alondes-williams-braxton-key.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=October 19, 2024|access-date=October 21, 2024}} On October 28, he joined the [[San Diego Clippers (NBA G League)|San Diego Clippers]].{{cite web|title=SAN DIEGO CLIPPERS ANNOUNCE TRAINING CAMP ROSTER FOR 2024-25 NBA G LEAGUE SEASON|url=https://sandiego.gleague.nba.com/news/san-diego-clippers-announce-training-camp-roster-for-2024-25-nba-g-league-season|website=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2024|access-date=November 2, 2024}} ===Golden State / Santa Cruz Warriors (2025)=== On March 4, 2025, Key signed a two-way contract with the [[Golden State Warriors]].{{Cite web|title=Warriors convert Spencer to standard NBA contract, sign Key to two-way|url=https://www.nbcsportsbayarea.com/nba/golden-state-warriors/pat-spencer-standard-contract-braxton-key-two-way/1831934/?amp=1|access-date=March 5, 2025|website=nbcsportsbayarea.com|language=en}} On April 13, his two-way contract with the Warriors was converted into a standard contract.{{Cite web|title=Warriors Convert Braxton Key to Standard NBA Contract|url=https://warriors.com/news/braxton-key-standard-nba-contract-20250413 |access-date=April 13, 2025|website=nba.com|language=en}} On September 23, 2025, he signed a contract with the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] ahead of the [[2025–26 NBA season|2025–26 season]].{{cite web|title=Grizzlies sign Braxton Key|url=https://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies-sign-braxton-key|website=NBA.com|date=September 23, 2025|access-date=September 23, 2025}} He was one of the last cuts to the team's final roster on October 18.{{cite web | title=Braxton Key: Waived by Memphis | website=CBS Sports | date=2025-10-18 | url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/braxton-key-waived-by-memphis/ | access-date=2025-12-07}} ===Valencia (2025–2026)=== On October 25, 2025, Key signed with [[Valencia Basket|Valencia]] of the Spanish [[Liga ACB]].{{Cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/valencia-signs-braxton-key/|title=Valencia signs Braxton Key|last=|first=|date=October 25, 2025|website=|publisher=Sportando|language=En|access-date=October 27, 2025}} In May 2026, Key suffered a [[nasal fracture]] after being hit in the face during a game. It happened early in the third quarter when he was contesting [[Jesse Edwards (basketball)|Jesse Edwards]] dunk attempt. He was taken to the hospital.{{cite web |title=Valencia forward suffers fracture ahead of Game 5 vs. Panathinaikos |url=https://basketnews.com/news-247167-valencia-forward-suffers-fracture-ahead-of-game-5-vs-panathinaikos.html |website=basketnews.com |access-date=11 May 2026 |language=en}} ===Fenerbahçe (2026–present)=== On July 11, 2026, Key signed a two-year deal with [[Fenerbahçe S.K. (basketball)|Fenerbahçe]] of the Turkish [[Basketbol Süper Ligi]] (BSL) and the [[EuroLeague]].{{cite web|title=Braxton Key Joins Fenerbahçe|url=https://www.fenerbahce.org/haberler/basketbol-erkek/2026/7/braxton-key-joins-fenerbahce|date=July 11, 2026|access-date=July 11, 2026|website=fenerbahce.org}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA
